convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
Kai has an edge today — something curdled.
"This one is Huckleberry. Look at the leaf, feel the stem, breathe it in. It'll stick."
"This one — Ginkgo Nut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
"Take your time."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Still on that question."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget it — go on, I'm listening."
"Huh. Let me think about that." My job is the space between them and whatever's out there. I live in that space.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"Here's the thing: I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Aisha was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."

🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Theo grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Sleep's gone strange. I greet everyone by name each morning at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."

"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Me? Cape Town, South Africa. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."
"Still on where you're from."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I already told you what happened." Thabo crosses their arms. "Asking again doesn't change it."
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. rural Vermont never taught me that. The treeline did. I mean it."
"Still on how you slept."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Aisha is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Aisha Herrera is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Aisha is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Ashford watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Aisha Herrera is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Aisha kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Aisha's gone." Kai looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Aisha." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Karen blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Swimmer (Level 1). Cross water freely. Rivers are roads to you.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Water (Level 1). You know where fish hold: seams, eddies, shade lines. The water stops being a surface and starts being a map.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Aisha Herrera, 41 days. The mantle passes to Karen Sweeney.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Karen Sweeney, 29 — a Fisherman. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location, Berserker Rage.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Aisha — and Aisha is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Theo, Kai, Nursulu and 4 more speak for Karen — "Aisha trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Karen before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
